purpose: Provenance manifest for one-way vendor-copies from the old SignalFrame repo (spec §3.1, §7.3). Every entry records the source commit, source path, target path, copy-time sha256, and adaptation note. The old repo is NEVER modified; copied code is maintained by this repo afterwards.
allowedSources: packages/crawler/src (SSRF/DNS-pinning crawl safety, static HTML fetch)
packages/audit/src/rules (implementations backing the 11 frozen MVP rules)

entries.adaptation: Vendored the IPv4 normalization and CIDR primitives, then expanded fail-closed RFC 6890 classification for special-use IPv4 and IPv6. IPv4-mapped IPv6 is recursively classified; only IPv6 global unicast 2000::/3 is eligible, with documentation, transition, translation, metadata, local, multicast, reserved, 6to4, and temporary-documentation ranges rejected.

Rewrote ./*.js import specifiers to ./*.ts. Preserves non-root trailing slashes because this layer owns exact transport identity; slash folding is confined to canonicalizeUrl(...).subjectUrl so fetchUrl remains traceable to the HTTP resource actually requested.

Rewrote ./*.js import specifiers to ./*.ts; added a finite injectable DNS lookup timeout, fixed non-sensitive failure reasons, validation of every returned address, literal-IP fast path, and fail-closed handling for empty, malformed, private, reserved, metadata, rebinding, and timed-out resolution results while preserving the guard-approved pinned address. Rejects non-standard HTTP(S) ports before DNS lookup or transport; only normalized default ports are admitted.
rewrote ./*.js import specifiers to ./*.ts; retained and exports the vendored pin-agent transport

vendored from source sha256 a925ebfddc72f8d7a209510d06237edccab356af0b7a8f10ca671803f8d57d02; rewrote the import specifier to TypeScript; pins a guard-approved IP through a per-request undici Agent; preserves the original hostname for Host, TLS SNI, and certificate validation; uses node:net isIP for the exact address family; strips IPv6 URL brackets; and omits SNI for IP-literal destinations

Rewrote ./*.js import specifiers to ./*.ts and expanded the vendor fixtures with public/private/special IPv4 and IPv6, multi-address rebinding, DNS failure/timeout, late-resolution isolation, hostname-safe errors, literal-IP bypass, timer-cleanup coverage, and pre-DNS rejection of non-standard HTTP(S) ports.

Vendored the regex HTML extraction helpers (attr/firstTag/tagText, heading/paragraph/anchor collection, JSON-LD walk) from page.ts plus extractNormalisedBody/decodeHtml from packages/crawler/src/extract.ts. HTML character references in href and canonical attributes are decoded before URL canonicalization, matching browser parsing so a standard `&` query separator cannot become a literal `amp;` parameter. Dropped all @signalframe/core types and inferPageRole (engine infers role later); dropped contentHash (crypto) and the date/claim-cue/image-alt observers not in the CrawlPageProjection contract. Reshaped output to the ParsedPage subset of CrawlPageProjection: persisted link targets remain canonical same-origin subject identities, while internal-link and canonical frontier targets preserve exact trailing-slash transport identity. Current crawl method v2 also persists the exact canonical fetch target instead of folding it to subjectUrl, so slash-only sitemap contradictions remain observable. Exact targets are capped at two per admitted subject; after the global subject budget is full, parsing continues only to retain a second exact variant for an already admitted subject, preventing both overflow and loss of the final slash sibling. Robots meta is parsed into robotsDirectives[]+robotsIndexable; jsonLd is reduced to {types,errorCount}; added bodyExcerpt and fixed count/element-length caps for every persisted title/meta/H1/heading/paragraph/outlink/anchor/rel/robots/JSON-LD projection, drops overlong URLs, bounds JSON-LD blocks/nodes with an iterative walk, and prioritizes critical robots directives before truncation; hardened hostile numeric HTML entities so invalid Unicode scalar values degrade to U+FFFD instead of aborting a crawl. Rewrote import specifiers to explicit .ts. Every fixed character cap is applied by CODE POINT rather than by UTF-16 code unit (`boundChars` in crawl/types.ts): a page title, heading, anchor or robots rule ending in an emoji is ordinary web input, and a cut between the halves of one character leaves an orphaned surrogate that PostgreSQL's jsonb refuses, so a completed crawl died on the write that stored its projection. The parser now also captures the factual `` declaration as ephemeral Crawl evidence, canonicalizes only valid BCP-47 tags, and keeps that fact outside the frozen page projection so a versioned site-language summary can be persisted without changing crawl.page.v1. decodeHtml then gained ', which it had always skipped even though HTML5 defines it and every browser resolves it. The gap only became visible once the sitemap parser learned the five XML predefined entities: a path written /o'neill resolved to one subject from a link and a different one from the sitemap, so the sitemap copy looked like a page nothing links to — the same false orphan_candidate that decoding work set out to remove. The two entrances to the frontier now agree on every named, numeric and nested reference, pinned by a cross-parser test in sitemap.test.ts. One deliberate exception remains:   is an HTML entity and not an XML one, so the page parser resolves it and the sitemap parser leaves it verbatim rather than inventing a character the document did not declare. decodeHtml was then rewritten from a chain of replaces into a single scan. The chain decoded its own output: < became < after the ampersand step and then < after the less-than step, handing back a character the document never wrote. That also split URLs in two once the sitemap parser moved to a single scan, because the same escape in an href and in a canonicalized to different subject URLs and the sitemap copy looked like a page nothing links to. On-page facts the upstream crawler has no equivalent for (Open Graph, Twitter card, viewport, charset, favicon, hreflang, image alt coverage, external-link rel/target safety, UTF-8 byte sizes) are collected here for the public On-Page Checker and returned as `ParsedPage.onPage`, deliberately outside `CrawlPageProjection` so the frozen `crawl.page.v1` metric the product persists is unchanged. Attribute reads walk the tag attribute by attribute instead of searching it for a name, because a name occurring inside another attribute's value (a Firebase image URL's `?alt=media`, a description mentioning `charset=utf-8`) was being read as that attribute; HTML comments are stripped once at entry so commented-out markup is not reported as present. Tag scanning then became quote-aware: `[^>]*` ended a tag at the first `>` in the source and `>` is ordinary text inside an attribute value, so `` was cut before `alt` and published as an image carrying no alt text. Script, style and template contents are removed once before any structural collector runs, because an inline template or a `document.write` string is markup to a regex and nothing at all to a reader; JSON-LD and byte sizes still read the document before that step, since one is about what a script block contains and the other about what was shipped. `` is now honoured, so relative links and canonical targets resolve where a browser resolves them instead of one directory too high. Alt text is entity-decoded before the emptiness test, `twitter:card` is accepted under `property=` as Twitter's own parser accepts it, and external links are deduplicated by canonical destination the way internal outlinks already were, with www and the apex treated as one site. Added on-page facts: declared image dimensions and lazy loading, script byte weight, interactive element counts, and whole-body text metrics (CJK code points, remaining whitespace runs, non-whitespace code points) so the audit can measure a body in units every script has instead of deciding the question from a 500-character sample. The body is also reduced to a repeated-phrase leaderboard here — one table per phrase length from one unit to five — because this is the only layer that still holds the whole text, and counting it downstream would give the leaderboard a different denominator from the length figure printed beside it.

Vendored parseGroups/globMatches/longest-match Allow-wins logic from robots.ts and the AI-crawler UA names from packages/crawler/src/ai-bots.ts (OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot). Dropped @signalframe/core CrawlerAccessRule and the monitored-bot report/kind taxonomy. Reshaped to CrawlRobotsProjection: projection.groups preserve every file user-agent group and guarantee an entry per required AI bot (resolved from its dedicated group else the * group). Added productToken() so the own-crawler gate matches 'SignalFrameBot/0.2' against a 'signalframebot' group; exposed isPathAllowed(groups,ua,path) + emptyRobots(). Added Crawl-delay: parseGroups now records a per-group crawlDelaySeconds and robotsCrawlDelaySeconds(groups,ua) resolves it with the same specificity rule as isPathAllowed, so a site that publishes its own rate ceiling is crawled at that rate rather than at our hardcoded floor. The value is clamped to 30s: the anonymous public tools run this crawler inside a synchronous serverless invocation, so an absurd or hostile Crawl-delay would otherwise spend the whole run waiting. Non-numeric, zero, and negative values are ignored.

Vendored the regex <loc> extraction + urlset/sitemapindex detection + decodeXml from sitemap.ts. Added index recursion, same-origin filtering, canonicalizeUrl-to-subjectUrl mapping, dedupe, and depth/document/url bounds, delegating HTTP to an injected fetchText so every fetch still passes the SSRF guard + shared budget. Output remains CrawlSitemapProjection {fetched,urlCount,subjectUrls}; an internal callback also emits exact fetch identities so the engine can retain slash and non-slash sitemap variants without changing the persisted projection contract. decodeXml was then widened from the three-entity chain (&/</>) to the five XML predefined entities plus numeric character references, in a single pass. XML permits & and & everywhere it permits &, and several generators emit them, so a numerically escaped query separator survived parsing as literal text; the resulting phantom URL canonicalized to something no page links to and surfaced as orphan_candidate (internal-link audit) and sitemap_page_without_observed_inlink (site audit) — parser artifacts reported as site findings. The single scan also fixes what a chain of replaces cannot: chained replaces decode their own output, so &#38; (a document asking for the literal text "&") became a bare ampersand. Unknown named entities are left verbatim rather than guessed at, since   is HTML and not XML, and hostile numeric references degrade to U+FFFD on the same posture as the page parser instead of aborting a crawl. Invalid numeric references then stopped degrading to U+FFFD: that quietly promoted malformed input into a brand-new same-origin URL, letting a sitemap declare thousands of distinct invalid suffixes that all entered the frontier and spent the crawl budget on targets the site never had. A <loc> carrying an out-of-range or surrogate reference is dropped instead. The rejection rule was then narrowed from "is a Unicode scalar" to XML 1.0's Char production: C0 controls and the noncharacters U+FFFE/U+FFFF are valid scalars and invalid XML, so accepting them still let a sitemap mint frontier entries out of references no conforming document could contain. Every boundary of Char round-trips, so the narrowing costs real sitemaps nothing.

Vendored the BFS loop, manual redirects, per-hop guard, pinned undici transport, byte-capped streaming body read, and host-delay pacing from crawl.ts. Retained CrawlFetcher as a fixture seam, while production enforces guard -> fresh createPinnedAgent -> undici fetch for every hop and closes both the response body and Agent after each hop. Dropped @signalframe/core SiteSnapshot/PageRecord/inferPageRole and the llms.txt + internal-link-depth analytics. Output reshaped to CrawlRaw; all CRAWL_BUDGET limits enforced (maxUrls/maxDepth/wall-clock/maxRedirects+SSRF re-check each hop/maxBodyBytes/perHostConcurrency/minHostDelay/robots), including a fixed 128 MiB total decoded-body run cap across robots, sitemaps, rejected responses, and pages. Every decoded chunk synchronously reserves from one shared remaining-byte budget before being accepted; the application-level usage never exceeds the cap, an over-budget body is discarded, other in-flight requests/readers are aborted or cancelled, and no new work launches. The cap has stable stopReason 'max_total_bytes', returns availability:'partial', and retains only pages completed within budget. Redirects fail closed before guard/transport on any origin change, and every page redirect target is checked against the same robots policy before transport. CrawlRaw now binds each record to the initial request identity: subjectUrl and projection.fetchUrl name the actual requested URL, status is the initial response, and finalStatus plus redirectChain retain the terminal journey facts. A terminal URL that is independently present in the frontier is fetched and persisted as its own direct record, so an alias status is never attached to the terminal SitePage. Exact request fetchUrl identities control transport/frontier deduplication and preserve slash semantics; downstream DiagnosticContext groups variants by subject while retaining every exact response. Sitemap scheduling first covers distinct bounded subjects, then spends remaining capacity on additional exact variants, so `/a/` cannot starve `/b`. Stream reader.read() and text()-fallback operations race the request/operation signal, consume late rejections, and use non-blocking best-effort cancel/drain/aborted close paths so hostile pending or throwing cancellation cannot defeat the wall-clock or external-abort boundary. URL-guard promises share the same bounded wall-clock/external-abort race, so a stalled DNS/SSRF guard cannot outlive worker shutdown. Guard, fetch, and abort failures use fixed internal kinds without evaluating or persisting dynamic guard/error/signal reasons. Added fixed persisted HTTP-header, robots, sitemap, rule, agent, and URL projection caps; on any budget cut returns partial with a specific stopReason and fills providerUsage plus a non-empty limitation. Guard and now remain injectable test seams; budget and maxRequests are trusted internal fixed-profile seams that public request paths may not control. The request cap covers robots, sitemap documents, page fetches, and redirects, reports the stable stopReason 'max_requests', and cannot launch transport after exhaustion. Every crawled URL and link target is canonicalized via canonicalizeUrl. Every fixed character cap is applied by CODE POINT rather than by UTF-16 code unit (`boundChars` in crawl/types.ts): a page title, heading, anchor or robots rule ending in an emoji is ordinary web input, and a cut between the halves of one character leaves an orphaned surrogate that PostgreSQL's jsonb refuses, so a completed crawl died on the write that stored its projection. The engine aggregates ephemeral per-page `<html lang>` evidence into one versioned site-language summary callback after Crawl completes, without adding unversioned fields to CrawlRaw or crawl.page.v1. robots.txt handling was then made to fail closed, per RFC 9309 2.3.1.4: an unreadable robots.txt (5xx, timeout, transport failure) now stops the crawl with stopReason robots_unreachable instead of substituting an empty ruleset and walking every disallowed path, while a 4xx still means no restrictions per 2.3.1.3. The unreachable branch is qualified on there being no prior stopReason, so a run whose byte budget, request cap, or abort signal already fired keeps its real reason. reachedNothing dropped its usage.urlsFetched === 0 term, which the robots and sitemap fetches satisfied before any page was considered and which therefore reported a site answering Disallow: / as availability available with a null stopReason; zero collected pages plus at least one robots refusal is now stopReason robots_disallowed and availability unavailable. The host pacer advances by the slower of budget.minHostDelayMs and the site's own Crawl-delay. Added a sleep seam beside the existing now seam so second-scale pacing is testable offline. The robots fetch then had to tell its two aborts apart: guardedFetch answers aborted both when the run's wall clock or caller signal ended everything and when only that one request timed out, and only the second is 'we could not read robots.txt'. Conflating them relabelled an ordinary max_duration stop as robots_unreachable and hid why the crawl really ended. The fetch now returns a distinct stopped kind for a run-level end, and the fail-closed stamp re-checks markOperationStop() at stamping time because the abort and the deadline land in either order on a loaded machine. Pacing then moved from once-per-queue-entry to once-per-wire-request via a pace hook on GuardedFetchDeps, so redirect hops, robots.txt and every sitemap document pay the host delay instead of going out free; the pacer is declared ahead of the robots fetch and starts at budget.minHostDelayMs, tightening to the site's Crawl-delay once that file has actually been read. The frontier's re-prioritisation dropped its per-link queue.findIndex scan for a pending Map keyed on fetch URL, which was O(N^2) in discovered links and turned an IO-bound crawl into a CPU-bound one with event-loop stalls that delayed the abort and deadline handling every other budget depends on. Deadline attribution hardened 2026-08-04: a request abort caused by the run's remaining wall clock now reports itself through makeRequestSignal's onRunDeadline callback, and deadlineHit() latches on it. Previously every consumer re-derived the deadline from a second Date.now() reading, which has millisecond resolution and is not monotonic — the timer armed for the deadline could fire while a fresh reading still sat below it, and the run then reported robots_unreachable (a claim about the site) for a crawl that had merely run out of time. An optional onPageProgress observation seam was added beside onSiteLanguageSummary: it fires from the single place a page record is accepted, carrying pagesCollected, which is the same quantity the finished CrawlRaw reports as pages.length and providerUsage.pagesCollected, so a synchronous caller can narrate a crawl in flight without keeping a counter of its own. It is observation only — a listener that throws is swallowed, and it can change neither the budget, the pacing, nor what is fetched. Carries `parsed.onPage` onto the page record beside the frozen `crawl.page.v1` projection, the same way `htmlLanguage` already travels beside it.
